title: What are the best sinister undercurrents in movies, something that is subtly alluded to, as opposed to outright shown?

commenti.body:
Don't know if this fits what you asked, but I always loved the scene toward the end of *Goodfellas* when Jimmy tries to have Karen walk back in that dark alleyway for some nice dresses he said he'd give her. She almost does but gets spooked when she looks in and sees some brutes standing in the shadows in hushed anticipation. Nothing is ever really stated or shown outright, but just hinted that if she had gone back in there she would not have come out alive.   


I just love the way Scorsese made it a more subtle thing than it could have been. It's so chilling. The scene starts off casually as two old friends having a chat and just subtly shifts into such a feeling of dread and darkness when Karen (and we) realize the score. Like, get the hell outta there girl, ain't *nothin*' good gonna happen in that alley lol.

Imagine that scene directed by Damien Chazelle. De Niro would twirl his moustache and wink into the camera and then Karen would let out a fart and go “did I do that?” and then a loud jazz score would play. Heh. Incompetency. Really tickles me purplE
